bullets.title: T: Blowout Q2 beat — JPM, KeyBanc, UBS, Citi all bullish; buyback raised to $10B
bullets.body: AT&T posted Q2 adj. EBITDA $12.34B (consensus $12.10B), EPS $0.65 vs. $0.59 est., and FCF $4.67B vs. $4.30B. Postpaid phone net adds 432K (est. ~330K) with churn 0.86%; fiber net adds 344K (est. 285K). Management raised 2026 buyback to $10B from $8B and plans $45B+ shareholder returns 2026-28. Multiple banks upgraded or reinforced Buy/OW: KeyBanc raised to OW ($36 PT), UBS upgraded to Buy, Citi maintains Buy ($31.50 PT), JPM maintains OW. Revenue missed slightly ($31.6B vs. $31.8B) and fiber ARPU declined 1.3% YoY on promos—key bear points.

bullets.title: SMCI: Record $60B orders and 15-17% gross margins vs. 8.2-8.4% guidance — stock +16% AH
bullets.body: Supermicro's FQ4 preliminary update showed revenue near the low end of $11–$12.5B guidance, but gross margins surged to 15–17% vs. prior 8.2–8.4% guide due to favorable customer/product mix. The company booked $60B+ in new Q4 orders (vs. $39B mid-quarter update), a record backlog. DELL and HPE followed SMCI higher. KeyBanc base case fair value $30 (11.9x FY27 EBITDA); Citi and JPM both maintain Neutral citing margin sustainability questions; Wolfe Peer Perform on governance/regulatory risk. Full earnings call August 11.

bullets.title: GOOGL earnings tonight: buyside Cloud growth >70% YoY, capex bar at $325-350B
bullets.body: Google reports after close with consensus EPS $2.88 and revenue $117B. Street expects ~65% Cloud growth; buyside bars are 70-75% YoY. JPM models 2027 capex at ~$300B (54% growth) vs. Street $250B; buyside bar $325-350B. Strong TPU revenue and Gemini 3.5 Pro launch timing also in focus. JPM tactically bullish and will turn bearish if capex is cut or buybacks reduced. Mizuho expects Cloud EBIT $7.1B vs. $6.9B consensus.

bullets.title: NVDA: Vera Rubin NVL72 launches with 10x token throughput/MW vs. Blackwell; CPO in volume production
bullets.body: NVIDIA unveiled the Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale system combining seven co-designed chips, delivering 10x higher token throughput per megawatt vs. GB200 NVL72 (800K vs. 80K tokens/s). The co-packaged optics (CPO) switch is described as in 'volume manufacturing'—bullish for LITE and AAOI. Wistron opened its $700M Fort Worth facility producing GB300 Grace Blackwell systems; Vera Rubin Superchip manufacturing cell being prepared. NVDA can reportedly produce 1,000 Vera Rubin racks/day (~$630B annual capacity). PyTorch Rubin (SM107) support added.

bullets.title: RDDT: -5.8% premarket on Google content-blocking report; GOOGL retaliation risk flagged
bullets.body: Reddit is considering restricting Google's access to its content for AI training. The $60M GOOGL AI deal (potentially 2-3x higher at renewal) is critical to the RDDT bull case. JPM Tech Sketch warns of traffic collapse if Google retaliates with an algorithm change, though the discussion is ongoing without a final decision.

bullets.title: Semis/memory premarket selloff: MU -4.5%, WDC -4.8%, INTC -4.0%, STX -3.8%
bullets.body: Broad semiconductor complex selling off ahead of the open with memory (MU -4.5%, WDC -4.8%, STX -3.8%) and networking names (CIEN -3.1%, LITE -2.8%) pressured. Equipment names AMAT and LRCX also down 3.7-4.1%. Nasdaq 100 futures -0.9% vs. settlement. Context: strong Tuesday rally (+5.2% SOX) is giving way to a risk-off tone as Iran/oil and Big Tech earnings uncertainty dominate.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM raises PT to $155, adds to Analyst Focus List ahead of 8/5 earnings
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised SHOP price target to $155 from $150 (OW) and added to its Analyst Focus List, projecting 2Q GMV growth of +29% and revenue growth of +30%. Chase Card data shows U.S. CNP growth of +11% in 2Q, accelerating vs. 1Q. European 2Q GMV grew +48% YoY (+35% FXN). Key risks: AI/LLM token costs add ~160bps headwind to Subscription Gross Margins (~40bps total), though FCF margin guided 18% (+60bps YoY).

bullets.title: META: Jefferies upgrades to Buy on AI glasses opportunity ($14-18B TAM); capex concerns from OPCO
bullets.body: Jefferies upgraded META to Buy citing $14-18B revenue opportunity from AI glasses (35-45M units at Apple Watch adoption rates), with ams OSRAM as key microLED supplier. Daily glasses users tripling YoY, 7M+ units in 2025. Separately, OPCO is cautious on META at Perform—sees capex needs at >$200B in 2027 (vs. Street $159B) to reach 14 GW target, and flags US time-spent growth slowing to +7% YoY vs. +17% in 2Q25. SemiAnalysis also reveals Meta's custom AMD MI400 chip at half MI455X size for recsys workloads.

bullets.title: INTC: SK Hynix Ohio fab talks — both companies deny outright sale, JV remains possible
bullets.body: Reports from JoongAng claimed SK Hynix in talks to acquire Intel's Ohio fab; both Intel and SK Hynix subsequently denied pursuing or deciding on an acquisition. Intel reaffirmed commitment to Ohio. One analyst notes neither company denied a possible joint venture structure. Intel also premarket -4% amid general semi weakness and Fortinet collaboration announcement.

bullets.title: CRWV: Upgraded to Buy at Truist ($126) and initiated at Outperform at Baird ($100)
bullets.body: CoreWeave received double upgrades post-close Tuesday—Truist upgraded to Buy from Hold with a $126 target and Baird initiated at Outperform with a $100 target. The stock traded +2.6% in after-hours and was +17% in overnight StreetAccount wrap. CRWV is deploying NVIDIA Spectrum-6 Ethernet switches as part of the Vera Rubin rollout.

bullets.title: NBIS: Baird initiates Outperform at $250; stock +119% YTD
bullets.body: Baird initiated Nebius Group at Outperform with a $250 price target, implying ~15% upside from $217. FactSet consensus average target is $270. NBIS has surged 119% YTD and was up 16% on the day reported.

bullets.title: LRCX preview: Citi Buy, models $145-250B WFE 2026-28, NAND structural demand from agentic AI
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on LRCX ahead of July 29 earnings. Agentic AI is driving structural NAND demand via KV cache offloading (reduces inference costs 20x), requiring 2-4 new greenfield fabs ($15-30B NAND WFE). Citi CY27/28 EPS estimates 3-8% above Street. Gross margin upside of ~30bps expected post-ASML's strong 54-57% Q3 guide. VAT Group's record CHF500M orders (+35% vs. consensus) also supportive of equipment cycle.

bullets.title: AEIS: Citi initiates Buy at $435; 800V DC TAM grows 20% CAGR to 2030
bullets.body: Citi initiated AEIS at Buy with $435 PT (32x CY27 EPS) ahead of August 3 earnings. Semi business forecast +23%/+27% YoY in CY26/27; Data Center +40%/+21%. The 800V DC transition creates a 20% CAGR SAM opportunity 2025-2030. Existing capacity supports $2.5B revenue with Thailand expansion extending to $4.5-5B. Morgan Stanley also has OW at $421 PT.

bullets.title: TKO: UBS Buy ($238 PT) on 40%+ FY26 EBITDA growth; GS Buy ($220 PT)
bullets.body: UBS maintains Buy on TKO with $238 PT, projecting FY26 revenues $5.77B and EBITDA $2.27B (+40%+), driven by new UFC Paramount deal, WWE Saudi Arabia site fees, and $75M IMG World Cup EBITDA contribution. GS separately maintains Buy ($220 PT) and expects 2Q revenue modestly above consensus but EBITDA slightly below from UFC Freedom 250 expenses.

bullets.title: GEV: Record 20 GW gas adds and raised 2030 capacity target; stock puzzled market despite beat
bullets.body: GE Vernova added 20 GW of gas SRAs+orders in Q2, exceeding the buyside ~18 GW bogey and raising its equipment-under-contract target from 110 to 125 GW and 2030 capacity target from 24 to 30 GW. Power EBITDA margin 18.8% (+100bps sequentially). Implied pricing $1,045/kW (up from $693 prior quarter). Only 2 of the 20 GW are confirmed orders; remainder are slot reservations. Stock sold off despite a strong print—OPCO notes market concerned by cycle durability.

bullets.title: CALX: Memory surcharge headwind bites; JPM cuts PT to $58 but keeps OW
bullets.body: CALX 2Q revenue beat ($293M vs. $293M guide top), but gross margin of 54.8% missed on higher-than-expected memory surcharges. 3Q guide gross margin 50.5-53.5% vs. JPM est. 55.2% — memory headwinds persist through 3Q. Software re-accelerated +7% QoQ. JPM cut PT to $58 from $65 but maintains OW at 12x 2028 earnings; Wolfe maintains Peer Perform citing muted margin bottom confidence.

bullets.title: ARM: MS reiterates Equal-Weight ($202 PT); stock doubled since March, limited 1Q27 upside
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains ARM at Equal-Weight with $202 PT. Infrastructure royalties expected to reach ~19% of royalty revenue (up from 14%) but smartphone royalties down 8% QoQ. Stock has more than doubled since the March 'Arm Everywhere' event and already reflects most of the 2030 CPU opportunity. 1Q27 EPS at lower end of guidance ($0.41); no formal CPU TAM guidance update expected.

bullets.title: TSLA: FSD 14.3.6 released; Vera Rubin Spectrum-6 adopter; Cybercab display at Tesla Diner
bullets.body: Tesla released FSD version 14.3.6 and is an early adopter of NVIDIA's Spectrum-6 102.4Tbps Ethernet switch for AI workloads. Cybercab on public display at Tesla Diner. TSLA reports earnings after close today.

bullets.title: MDB: DDOG replacing MongoDB with Postgres in some deployments — stock -5% premarket
bullets.body: JPM Tech Sketch flagged DataDog is replacing MongoDB with Postgres in some customer deployments, sending MDB down ~5% premarket. Piper separately notes infrastructure software (TEAM, MDB, SNOW) can cut customer token costs 50-75% while improving AI accuracy, positioning them as picks-and-shovels for the AI compute efficiency wave.

bullets.title: HOOD: KeyBanc raises PT; prediction market revenue expected to exceed crypto revenue in Q2
bullets.body: KeyBanc raised HOOD price target and is comfortable owning shares ahead of earnings. Bernstein and Piper Sandler expect prediction market revenue to exceed crypto revenue in Q2 for the first time. CLARITY Act passage (now ~46% on Polymarket) is an upside catalyst for HOOD and COIN. KeyBanc notes lagging crypto volume through July creates 2H downside risk.
